title: Recurring deposits & savings plans
examples: How do I find the final amount if I save money every month?
What is the difference between simple interest and interest on recurring deposits?
Can you show me an example of calculating the total interest earned?

explain.say: Today we learn about recurring deposits and savings plans. This means saving a fixed amount regularly. We want to find the total money you will have later. This final amount is called the maturity value.
The interest you earn is not just on the last deposit. You earn interest on all the money you put in over time. This is different from simple interest. We need a special formula for this.
Let us say you deposit ten pounds every year for three years. The first deposit earns interest for three years. The last deposit earns interest for just one year.

items: Year 1 Deposit: Earns interest for 3 years
Year 2 Deposit: Earns interest for 2 years
Year 3 Deposit: Earns interest for 1 year

explain.say: The maturity value is the sum of all your deposits plus all the interest earned. You can use a specific formula involving the interest rate and the number of payments. This gives you the total amount at the end.

items: Formula uses interest rate and payments

faq.q: What is the difference between a recurring deposit and a regular savings account?
faq.a: A recurring deposit usually means you commit to depositing a fixed amount at set intervals. A regular savings account might allow more flexible deposits. Both help you save money over time.
asks: Is it the same as a fixed deposit?

faq.q: Do I always earn interest on the very first deposit?
faq.a: Yes, every deposit you make earns interest for the time remaining until the maturity date. The earlier you deposit, the more interest you earn.
asks: Does the first payment earn interest?
How long does the first payment earn interest for?

faq.q: Is the interest calculated on the total amount I deposit?
faq.a: No, the interest is calculated on the amount deposited for the specific time period it remains in the account. It is not simply on the total sum.
asks: Is it simple interest or compound?
Does interest build up over time?

faq.q: What do I need to know to calculate the maturity value?
faq.a: You need the fixed deposit amount, the interest rate per period, and the total number of periods. These three values are essential for the calculation.

faq.q: If the interest rate changes, does it affect the maturity value?
faq.a: Yes, the interest rate is a key component of the calculation. A change in the rate will change the total interest earned and thus the maturity value.
asks: How does the interest rate affect the final amount?

facts: A recurring deposit requires making equal payments at regular intervals.
The maturity value is the total sum received at the end of the plan.
Interest is calculated on the principal amount for the time it is held.
The interest earned increases as the deposit period gets longer.

quiz.say: If you deposit ten pounds yearly for two years at zero percent interest, what is the maturity value?
quiz.why: Since there is no interest, the maturity value is simply the sum of all deposits, which is ten plus ten.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you are not depositing one hundred pounds total.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it suggests the interest calculation is more complex than it needs to be.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it only counts the first deposit and ignores the second one.

quiz.say: A person deposits fifty pounds every six months for four years at a rate of four percent per year. What is the total amount deposited?
quiz.show: Total Deposits = Payments x Number of Payments
quiz.why: The total amount deposited is found by multiplying the fixed payment by the total number of payments made over the years.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it multiplies the payment by the number of years instead of the number of payments.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it only calculates the deposit for two years instead of four.
wrong.2: This is wrong because it incorrectly adds the interest amount to the total deposits.

quiz.say: If you deposit twenty pounds annually for three years at a rate of eight percent interest, what is the total interest earned?
quiz.why: You must first calculate the maturity value using the formula, and then subtract the initial deposits to find only the interest earned.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it incorrectly assumes the interest earned is equal to the total deposits.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it calculates the interest as if it were simple interest on the total sum.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it only calculates the interest on the first deposit for three years.
